title: Excess type I interferon disrupts developmental crosstalk and promotes premature distalization in trisomy 21 lungs
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79210-4

Congenital lung anomalies are associated with Trisomy 21 lungs. Here, authors show that hyperactivation of the type I IFN signaling pathway promotes precocious epithelial cell differentiation, contributing to the T21 related lung pathologies.

title: Spatiotemporal modulation of microalgae to boost biofuel generation from CO<sub>2</sub> by the stick-to-culture strategy
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79326-7

Balancing biomass growth and lipid accumulation remains a challenge in microalgal biofuel production. Here the authors report extracellular matrix-mimicking hydrogel scaffolds that dynamically reconfigure the microenvironment of spatially organized microalgae, allowing controlled switching between the two states.

title: Metabolic reprogramming modulates cardiomyocyte hypertrophy via GLS1 in chronic kidney disease in male mice
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79129-w

Chronic kidney disease often causes heart enlargement, a serious complication whose mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that excess phosphate activates the metabolic enzyme GLS1, promoting heart enlargement, while blocking GLS1 protects against this effect in male mice.

title: The gene ivory:mir-193 controls scale type differentiation in Heliconius butterflies
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79315-w

Butterfly wing scales are diverse cell types that generate the colours and structures used in communication and adaptation. This study shows that the non-coding RNA ‘ivory’ controls alternative scale-cell states, linking regulatory evolution to phenotypic diversity.

title: Li<sup>+</sup>-locked domain effect for breaking the temperature stability bottleneck in thermal-detection high-entropy energy storage ceramics
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79179-0

Dielectric energy-storage ceramics lose polarization at high temperatures, limiting harsh-environment use. Here, the authors show a Li+- locked domain effect in high-entropy BNT-based ceramics, achieving Wrec = 11.43 J cm−3, η = 84.67%, Δη/η < 0.3% up to 320 °C, with self-diagnostic thermometry.

title: Volumetric scattering microscopy
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79103-6

Volumetric scattering microscopy (VSM) enables non-invasive and scan-free 3D fluorescence imaging through scattering biological tissues, allowing clearer visualization across multiple scales, including cells, tissues, and intact organisms.

title: Small-molecule targeting of kinesin-13 KIF2C enhances double-strand break DNA repair and slows down aging
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79165-6

DNA damage is associated with aging and premature aging disorders. Here, the authors show that small molecule activation of the kinesin-13 KIF2C improves double-strand break DNA repair in aged cells and extends lifespan in progeria mice.

title: PRMT1 methylates SKP1 to inhibit the ubiquitination of pro-proliferative phosphoproteins during hepatocyte proliferation
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79101-8

During liver regeneration, EGF upregulates PRMT1, leading to increased asymmetric arginine dimethylation at R81 of SKP1. This impedes the interaction between SKP1 and FBXW7, protects pro-proliferative phosphoproteins from ubiquitin-mediated degradation, and thereby maintains hepatocyte proliferation.
